subject: Next steps: payment route evaluation & security gating for Beacon Labs
thread_content:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Barnes <leah@beaconlabs.com>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@beaconlabs.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: payment route evaluation & security gating for Beacon Labs

Leah / Sara — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so procurement can decide on the most efficient payment path: PO (paper process), credit card, or marketplace listing.

Recap (from our demo):
- Beacon Labs wants predictable latency for inference and VPC controls for sensitive data.
- Main procurement blockers: internal PO approval, SOC 2 evidence, signed DPA, and a short security questionnaire from Infosec.

Options we discussed:
1) Purchase Order (PO) - Standard for larger contracts. We can accommodate net-30 invoicing and provide monthly invoices and W-9. Requires an executed DPA + SOC 2 report before finance signs.
2) Credit card - Fastest to get started (self-serve) but not typical for committed reserved capacity.
3) Marketplace (cloud partner) - Eases procurement for some customers; introduces third-party billing fees and a modest delay while the marketplace listing is provisioned.

What we need from Beacon to unblock procurement:
- Confirm primary payment preference (PO vs card vs marketplace).
- Procurement form (if PO) and any internal PO routing contacts.
- Security questionnaire (we can pre-fill the standard sections).

What Redwood will provide immediately:
- SOC 2 summary + full report on request (I attached the pre-release summary; full report available under NDA).
- Redwood DPA draft for signature (attached).
- Short answers doc for the 3rd-party security questionnaire (we'll return within 48 business hours).

Attachments: SOC2_report_2026.pdf (summary), Redwood_DPA_v3.docx

Next step suggestion: Sara, if procurement can share the Beacon procurement form and confirm preferred payment route, we'll turn around a tailored commercial path and a DocuSign link for the DPA. If you prefer marketplace, we can also flag that to partnerships and give an ETA for listing.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Next steps: payment route evaluation & security gating for Beacon Labs

Quick answers:
- PO workflow: Redwood accepts Beacon's PO form; standard processing is net-30, invoices issued monthly unless Beacon requests an annual invoice. Finance can accept electronic POs and will map to the deal id.
- Marketplace option: we can route billing through our AWS/Azure marketplace partners which often removes the PO friction for some procurement teams — tradeoff is marketplace fees (typically 5-10%) and a slightly different onboarding path. If Beacon is open to marketplace, we can expedite start-of-service within ~2 weeks after getting the listing request in.
- Discounts: For annual committed volumes we can offer a 5% prepay or PO discount; for monthly invoicing, discounts are smaller.
- DPA / DocuSign: I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope for Redwood_DPA_v3.docx once procurement confirms the PO route.

Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-9876 (added Beacon to the pipeline)

3) Commercial: Karthik to issue draft invoice cadence options and confirm whether Beacon prefers monthly or annual invoicing (Deliver by: 2027-04-08)
4) Marketplace: If Beacon prefers marketplace to bypass PO, confirm and we'll loop Partnerships (ETA listing: ~2 weeks). Owner: Karthik / Partnerships

I've attached the SOC 2 summary we discussed. I'll send the DocuSign for the DPA once procurement confirms they will sign the DPA in standard form (we can accept reasonable redlines).

Attachments referenced: SOC2_report_2026.pdf (summary), Redwood_DPA_v3.docx (will be DocuSigned)

Best — Hannah
